question: How can zirconium metal-organic framework materials be modified to improve ion adsorption capacity and selectivity?
answer: The ion adsorption capacity and selectivity of zirconium metal-organic frameworks (Zr-MOFs) can be improved through several strategies: (1) modifying the MOF frameworks with functional groups (e.g., -NH2, -SH, -COOH, -OH, -SO4) to enhance ion-binding interactions; (2) developing hybrid materials by integrating Zr-MOFs with polymers or graphene oxide (GO) to optimize adsorption performance; and (3) designing new Zr-MOFs with tailored pore structures and functional units for selective ion capture. Additionally, stimuli-responsive ligands can enable controlled ion release, while functionalized Zr-MOF membranes (e.g., with -NO2, -SH) improve ion sieving selectivity. Computational modeling of structure-performance relationships further aids in optimizing Zr-MOFs for efficient ion separation.

The paper aims to review recent advancements in the development and application of zirconium metal-organic framework (Zr-MOF) materials for ion adsorption and ion sieving in industrial separation processes.
